title: Confirm TrackManagementBody is wired into a real screen — it currently has zero callers in lib/

evidence.quote:
const widget = TrackManagementBody(showBackButton: false);
          expect(widget.showBackButton, isFalse);

bool trackDeletionAllowed({required int activeCurriculumCount}) {
  return activeCurriculumCount > 1;

why: TrackManagementBody's own doc comment says it unifies 'both parent and child track-management screens.' grep -rn "TrackManagementBody" lib/ finds only its own definition file — no @RoutePage() screen, and no entry in the generated app_router.gr.dart, ever instantiates it. The actual routed hub screen, track_management_hub_screen.dart (340 lines, near-identical import list), is a separate hand-rolled implementation with its own 'TS-16' deactivation guard (trackDeletionAllowed) — the exact concept Story 26.22 AC2 put in the service layer — and it was touched by a later bug-fix wave ('fix(tracks-scheduler): fix all 8 confirmed-bug clusters TS-1 through TS-16', 2026-06-11) that track_management_body.dart never received (last touched 2026-05-20, a mechanical colour-literal pass). The acceptance test only constructs TrackManagementBody in isolation and reads a constructor field, so it reports Story 26.22's central claim as verified while the shipped app still runs a duplicate, drifting implementation — and if TrackManagementBody is ever wired in later without reconciling the drift, it will reintroduce the 8 bugs TS-1..TS-16 fixed only in the hub screen.
recommendation: Either finish the consolidation — replace track_management_hub_screen.dart's build() with TrackManagementBody(showBackButton: ...) and delete the duplicated logic (carrying the TS-1..TS-16 fixes into the shared widget) — or, if the widget was superseded, delete the dead track_management_body.dart and this test. Add a source-grep assertion (matching the pattern already used in 26.20 AC3/4) proving the real screen references TrackManagementBody(.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'TrackManagementBody(' lib/features/ matches at least one real @RoutePage() screen's build method
a story-acceptance test asserts track_management_hub_screen.dart's source contains 'TrackManagementBody(', the same way 26.20 AC4 checks settings_screen.dart
the TS-16 deactivation guard logic exists in exactly one place, not duplicated between the widget and the hub screen

corrections: Evidence cites track_management_hub_screen.dart:24 but the quoted function signature/body actually sits at lines 25-26; line 24 is the last line of the preceding doc comment. Quote text itself is verbatim-accurate, just off by one line.
